title: Consistency vs Availability
subtitle: During a partition, price a wrong answer against no answer, and split the choice by data
motto: Ask what a wrong answer costs before you decide a slow one is worse
keyInsight: Consistency wins when one wrong answer costs more than the sales you lose by refusing to answer, which at a 2% oversell rate is basket size divided by 0.02.

decisions.title: Make the break-even the output
decisions.description: The calculator reports the cost per oversold order at which the answer flips, so the choice becomes a number to compare with your own business.
decisions.alternatives: Declaring a winner for e-commerce would hide that the same calculation picks the opposite side for payments.

decisions.title: Include the hybrid
decisions.description: The last frame refuses only orders on nearly sold-out items, since real systems choose per operation, not for the whole site.
decisions.alternatives: Offering only the two pure options would suggest the choice is all or nothing.
